qt: to the Commission Nikos Pappas (The Left) Subject:

Multiple sclerosis is often accompanied by invisible symptoms, such as fatigue, cognitive dysfunctions and chronic pain, which act as barriers to employment and social participation. The Greek Multiple Sclerosis Society has highlighted the need for these symptoms to be taken into account more fully and to support sufferers more effectively. Articles 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union prohibits discrimination while Article 26 provides for the integration of persons with disabilities under EU law. Council Directive 2000/78/EC provides for equal treatment in employment and for reasonable accommodation. Directive (EU) 2024/2841 establishes the European Disability Card and provides for the involvement of representative organisations in its implementation. The enhanced Strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities up to 2030 sets out the priorities in this area. In view of the above, can the Commission say: 1.
What actions is it planning as part of the enhanced strategy, to remove barriers to the social and professional lives of people with invisible disabilities?
What initiatives does it intend to take to further promote the implementation of Article 5 of Directive 2000/78/EC, in particular with regard to reasonable accommodation in the workplace?
How does it intend to support the active involvement of representative organisations, as provided for in Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2024/2841, in the implementation of the European Disability Card?
